title: squalify must stay exact up to its caps and approximate deterministically beyond them, in bounded memory
lead: When a cap is crossed, the sketch absorbs the exact buffer in input order. Memory accounting is added, along with tests on generated streams: 256 MB in CI, and 4 GB run manually.
boundary: **Not in this slice:** the HLL++ empirical bias tables; parallel accumulation.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
Goals: a full streaming scan with bounded memory, and determinism.

Owner decisions (2026-10-13): the caps as drafted, an in-repo xxHash64, and byte-identical output across OS and CPU, using `DetMath` instead of `Math.Log`.

Both sketches are deterministic for a fixed hash and input order:
- HLL takes the max of its registers, so its estimate does not depend on input order. Its relative error is 1.04/√m.
- GK has no randomness, and its rank error is at most εN.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- `src/squalify/Sketches/HyperLogLog.cs`: m = 16,384 byte registers.
  - The index is the top 14 bits of `XxHash64(value)`. The rank is `BitOperations.LeadingZeroCount` of the remaining bits plus 1.
  - The raw estimate is α_m·m²/Σ2^−M[j], with the powers of two from `Math.ScaleB`, which is exact.
  - Linear counting, m·`DetMath.Ln`(m/V), is used when E ≤ 2.5m and V > 0.
  - The result is rounded to a long using `Math.Round` with `MidpointRounding.ToEven`.
- `src/squalify/Sketches/GreenwaldKhanna.cs`: insert, and compress on the fixed schedule of every ⌊1/(2ε)⌋ inserts. A query returns a stored value.
- `FieldAccumulator`: when a cap is crossed, it feeds the exact buffer to the sketch in input order and frees the buffer. The output gets `approximate: true` and an `errorBound`: relative 1.04/√m for distinct counts, and εN ranks for quantiles.
- `MemoryBudget`: each accumulator gets an `EstimatedBytes` figure. `MemoryBudget.CeilingBytes` = the sum of the accumulators' `EstimatedBytes` + a fixed allowance for the runtime and I/O buffers. The allowance is documented in `docs/design.md` "Bounded memory and sketches"; the owner confirms its number before the slice starts. sq-19 asserts against the same ceiling.
- `tests/squalify.Tests/Sources/SyntheticCsvSource.cs`: an `IProfileSource` that generates N rows × M columns of mixed types on the fly, from a seeded xorshift generator. Nothing is written to disk.
- `docs/design.md` "Bounded memory and sketches"; `docs/how-it-works.md` section 5.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
1. `Hll_ErrorWithin3Sigma_On1MDistinct`.
2. `Hll_SameSetDifferentOrder_SameEstimate`.
3. `Hll_SmallRange_LinearCounting`.
4. `Gk_RankErrorWithinEpsilonN` on 10M values.
5. `CapCrossing_Boundary` (theory: cap−1, cap, cap+1 give exact, exact, approximate).
6. `Approximate_FlaggedWithErrorBound`.
7. `MemoryAccounting_UnderBudget_256MbStream`, run in CI.
8. `[Trait("Category","Large")] Memory_4GbStream_PeakWorkingSetBounded`: manual only; peak working set ≤ `MemoryBudget.CeilingBytes`. CI runs with `--filter Category!=Large`.
9. `Sketch_Goldens_SameBytesOnAllOs`.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
1. Write the tests.
2. Implement HLL, then GK, then the crossover, then the accounting.
3. Update the CI workflow's test filter.
4. Mutation checks: seed the hash randomly, and test 9 must go red. Swap `DetMath.Ln` for `Math.Log`, and confirm on CI that the goldens are still pinned, noting in the PR which platforms were checked.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
- `dotnet build squalify.sln -c Release`
- `dotnet test squalify.sln -c Release`
- `dotnet format squalify.sln --verify-no-changes`
- One manual run of `dotnet test --filter Category=Large`, with peak memory and duration recorded in a slicer note.
- If this slice changed architecture (the pipeline, an interface, a descriptor section or a determinism rule), `docs/how-it-works.md` and its diagrams are updated and `./scripts/render-docs.sh` has been re-run. The architect confirms there is no drift.
- `slicer check`

sections.heading: Git
sections.body: Worktree `.worktrees/sq-11` on branch `sq-11`. No agent commits. After the gate returns `VERDICT: PASS`, the orchestrator commits `sq-11: sketches and memory bounds` when the owner approves.
